body:
## Pull request overview

This PR implements persistence for app metadata during creation and editing by integrating `client.meta.saveItem()` calls. Previously, apps created or edited through the wizard would vanish on browser refresh because the converted schema was never saved to the backend.

**Changes:**
- Wires `client.meta.saveItem('app', name, schema)` into `CreateAppPage` and `EditAppPage` completion handlers to persist app metadata before navigation
- Adds MSW PUT handlers for `/meta/:type/:name` and `/metadata/:type/:name` endpoints to enable metadata persistence in mock/dev mode
- Updates test suite with `getClient()` mock and two new integration tests verifying `saveItem` is called on create and edit completion

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 5 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| apps/console/src/pages/CreateAppPage.tsx | Added adapter import and `client.meta.saveItem()` call in `handleComplete` to persist app metadata on creation |
| apps/console/src/pages/EditAppPage.tsx | Added adapter import and `client.meta.saveItem()` call in `handleComplete` to persist app metadata on edit |
| apps/console/src/mocks/handlers.ts | Added PUT handlers for both `/meta/:type/:name` and `/metadata/:type/:name` endpoints delegating to `protocol.saveMetaItem` |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/app-creation-integration.test.tsx | Extended `MockAdapterInstance` with `getClient()` stub and added two integration tests asserting `saveItem` calls |
| ROADMAP.md | Updated P1.11 section to document the new metadata persistence feature and test count |
</details>

Code duplication: The handlers for both endpoints (meta and metadata) contain identical logic. This duplication violates DRY principles and makes maintenance harder. Consider extracting the handler logic into a shared function that both endpoints can use, or document why both endpoints are needed if they serve different purposes in production vs development environments.

Test verification issue: The test retrieves the client and verifies the mock was called, but it doesn't verify that the saveItem call happened during the handleComplete execution. The test could pass even if saveItem was called at a different time or in a different context. Consider using vi.clearAllMocks() before the test interaction and then asserting that saveItem was called exactly once, or use toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) to ensure it was called the expected number of times.

Test verification issue: Similar to the create app test, this test doesn't verify that the saveItem call happened during the handleComplete execution and could pass even if saveItem was called at a different time. Consider using vi.clearAllMocks() before the test interaction and then asserting that saveItem was called exactly once, or use toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) to ensure it was called the expected number of times.
